subject.title: [Feature]: openclaw models status --probe --all — per-model health check across all configured models

question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit live `models status --probe --all` CLI mode that probes every configured model, with quota/rate-limit safeguards and the existing one-model probe left unchanged by default?
rationale: The requested behavior is technically plausible and source-reproducible, but it is a new live provider-request mode that can consume quota and change user expectations for auth/model health diagnostics.

options.title: Add explicit all-model probe
options.body: Implement `--probe --all` as an opt-in CLI mode with provider/profile filters, bounded concurrency/timeouts, JSON output, and clear quota/rate-limit messaging.

options.title: Fold into fallback-health work
options.body: Track this under a broader fallback-chain validation design if maintainers want one health-check workflow rather than another `models status` mode.

options.title: Leave to docs/manual checks
options.body: Keep `models status --probe` as a provider/auth check and document manual per-model validation for users with large custom model lists.

recommendation.title: Add explicit all-model probe
recommendation.body: Implement `--probe --all` as an opt-in CLI mode with provider/profile filters, bounded concurrency/timeouts, JSON output, and clear quota/rate-limit messaging.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history ties the auth/model probe regression and provider routing work to this owner, and the decision affects provider/auth CLI behavior.
